title: Indian diaspora schedules protest in London over voter rolls

tea.why: Protesters gathered over alleged irregularities in India's electoral rolls and the Special Intensive Revision.
tea.want: Demonstrators demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
tea.changed: Oct 17: A crowd gathered at Parliament Square in London for a protest and a counter-protest.

summary: Members of the Indian diaspora and supporters gathered at Parliament Square in London, United Kingdom, to voice opposition against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls and the Special Intensive Revision. YouTuber Dhruv Rathee had called on people to assemble near the Mahatma Gandhi statue in Parliament Square to bring international attention to the issue. Concurrently, supporters of the Chief Election Commissioner and Prime Minister Narendra Modi organized a counter-protest at the location. Organizations such as the Students' Federation of India, United Kingdom, also participated by gathering outside the High Commission of India to voice demands for the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
organizers: Students' Federation of India, United Kingdom
demands: Resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: A crowd and a counter-protest gathered at Parliament Square in London regarding voter roll issues.
